Adding a quick ops snapshot from infra (initial findings):
- Dedicated pool for LedgerOne hit sustained 92% GPU queue utilization between 08:33-08:58 PT.
- KV cache hit-rate for hot prefixes dropped from 86% -> 52% over the same window (see kv-cache-hitrate.csv).
- We saw an increase in short-lived cold-start sequences; model KV churn explains elevated memory pressure and token dispatch latency.
- No host OOMs; networking and host-level metrics OK; contention looks to be at the serving runtime level (scheduling + KV cache pressure).

Recommended immediate actions (ops):
1) Authorize emergency burst: +40% throughput to dedicated pool for 4 hours (auto-revoke) to blunt customer impact.
2) Apply temporary routing rule: fall back LedgerOne prod route to q4-86-lite for non-critical endpoints for the next 2 hours.
3) Enable aggressive KV prefetch for 15m to recover hit-rate.

Cost / trade-offs: burst will increase short-term cost (~$2.8k estimate for 4h) and may reduce headroom for other non-reserved users; we can limit to LedgerOne-specific reservations if approved.

Attachments: ops-metrics-0404.png (heap/queue graphs), kv-cache-hitrate.csv.

Asking for Vivek / David quick sign-off so we can announce to LedgerOne and start the bridge — customers are seeing business impact now.
